_what: Every published Sites app also works inside AI apps (ChatGPT, Claude and any app that speaks the MCP Apps standard) with no work from its maker: its own address answers MCP at `path` (src/public-app-mcp.mjs, routed by src/public-app-host.mjs answerPublicApp). `view` is the one ui:// view the open tool names, drawn from the app's home page by parts/ui/show/ai-app-bridge/ai-app-site-page.mjs. `tools` are the fixed names the server gives its open, list-pages, read-page and request tools (an underscore never appears in a placement id, so they never collide with the maker's own forms, whose placement ids name their tools). `pages` bounds the read road that lets an AI read the site's own pages with no screen: `media_types` are the kinds of file that count as a readable page (the plain ones read as plain text), `not_pages` are the address prefixes the host answers itself rather than from stored pages, `max_pages` is the most pages one list answer holds (`max_listing_reads` bounds the stored-file reads behind it), `title_bytes` is how much of each page is read to find its title, `read_bytes` the most of one page read, `max_text_characters` and `max_links` the most words and links handed back, and `max_redirects` how many same-site redirects a read follows. `field_schemas` turns each visitor-action field type (src/public-app-definition.mjs) into the JSON Schema an AI app reads; a new field type is one row here. `request` bounds what the page inside the chat may ask of its own app through the request tool: the methods a visitor's browser could use there, the largest body, and the largest answer handed back. `words` are what the AI and the person read; {name} is the app's name, {title} a form's title and {address} the app's web address.

words.instructions: {name} is a site made with Trillion at {address}. You can read it: list_pages gives the address and title of each of its pages, search_pages finds words across them, and read_page gives the words on one page and the pages it links to. When you answer from the site, say which page address you read. open_site shows the site to the person here, live, and each other tool sends one of its forms for the person, the same as sending it on the site.
words.list_description: Lists the pages of {name} you can read, each with its address and title. If the answer says there are more, call it again with that value as after.
words.listed: {name} has {count} pages to read. Made with Trillion.
words.listed_none: {name} has no pages to read yet.
words.more_after: There are more pages. Call list_pages again with after set to {after}.
words.read_description: Reads one page of {name} and gives you its words, with its headings on their own lines, and the pages it links to. Give an address from list_pages, or a path such as /about. Say which page address you read when you answer.
words.page_outside: Only pages of this site can be read here.
words.page_missing: This page was not found. Use list_pages to see the pages you can read.
words.page_not_readable: This address is not a page with words to read.
words.open_description: Shows {name} in this chat, live: its pages, pictures and forms, the same as at {address}. Use it whenever the person wants to see or use {name}.
words.opened: {name} is open below. Made with Trillion.
words.action_description: Sends the {title} form on {name} for the person, exactly as sending it on the site would. Ask the person for anything they did not already give.
words.run_description: Runs {title} on {name} for the person, exactly as using it on the site would.
words.request_description: For the page of {name} shown in this chat only: one request the page makes to its own site. An AI never calls it; open_site shows the site.
words.already_sent: {name} already had this answer; nothing was sent twice.
words.outside_request: This page can only reach its own site.
words.too_large: This is too large to send from a chat.
words.unavailable: This site is unavailable right now. Try again in a moment.
words.policy_invalid: The site’s AI page settings are invalid. The site owner needs to correct .well-known/trillion-ai.json.
words.search_description: Searches a bounded page of this site’s public words, returning matching page addresses and excerpts. Continue with more_after until it is null. Cite the returned page addresses.
words.search_words: Give between 1 and 300 characters to search for.
words.search_more: More pages remain to search. Call search_pages again with the same words and after set to {after}.
